problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of f: ℝ^d → ℝ, permitting nonconvex objectives. The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz, and a global lower bound satisfies f(x0) − lower ≤ Δ. Parameters require L > 0 and Δ ≥ 0.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Worker i evaluates g_i(x, ξ), with E[g_i(x, ξ)] = ∇f(x) and E‖g_i(x, ξ) − ∇f(x)‖² ≤ σ². Worker distributions may differ. Samples are IID within each worker and independent across worker streams. Replies contain the queried point and stochastic gradient; no Hessian or function-value oracle is supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean: system and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean: IsStochasticGradient; LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean: ComputeQuery and ComputeReply.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform second-moment noise bound σ² at every query point, with σ ≥ 0. No exponential-tail or samplewise smoothness condition is imposed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean: IsStochasticGradient.variance_integrable and variance; LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), with d a natural number.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details:
The gradient is differentiable and its derivative satisfies ‖D∇f(x) − D∇f(y)‖ ≤ Q‖x − y‖ globally, with Q ≥ 0. All parameters, including Q, L, Δ, σ, ε, x0 and network costs, are public.
Elapsed-time model with one server and n ≥ 1 workers in a star network. Worker i needs h_i > 0 time per gradient and has at most one pending computation. Each directed server–worker link has at most one pending message; distinct links operate concurrently. A message takes l + b times its transmitted bit length, including a 64-bit execution-added suffix. Algorithms use 64-bit clock readings, may abort computations, and must have almost surely finitely many events through the deadline.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence:
LongTails/Setups/DistributedHessianLipschitzNonconvex.lean: Params.Q and spec fields Public, publicInput, valid, admissible.
LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean: computation and communication; LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean: clockBits, Algorithm, step, FiniteEvents and TimedConvergence; LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean: Params and spec.valid.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The output is a measurable ℝ^d-valued random point with integrable gradient norm satisfying E‖∇f(output)‖ ≤ ε, where ε > 0. The norm is not squared.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over the product of the algorithm seed law and oracle seed law, for the server-designated output at the fixed elapsed-time deadline.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean: law, execute and TimedConvergence; LongTails/Setups/DistributedHessianLipschitzNonconvex.lean: spec.successful.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Smooth stochastic nonconvex stationarity with a Lipschitz Hessian is established, but this setup specifies a detailed elapsed-time benchmark with concurrent star links, finite bitstrings, latency, per-bit costs, and finite clock readings.
